    Occurrence bases for minimal right almost-split maps #

    For a chosen indecomposable decomposition of the middle term of a minimal right almost-split map, this file constructs the coordinate map from copies of one indecomposable to the linear irreducible-morphism space Irr = rad / rad². Right minimality proves linear independence, while scalar endomorphisms of the source prove spanning. Thus the multiplicity of an indecomposable middle summand is exactly the dimension of the corresponding irreducible-morphism space.

    The construction is abstract: it uses no quiver presentation or module classification, and it applies to projective-boundary right almost-split maps as well as to almost-split sequences.

                        Occurrence classes are linearly independent for every minimal right almost-split decomposition. Right minimality alone eliminates a hypothetical radical-square relation, so this argument also covers projective boundary maps and needs no AR kernel or translation data.
